body.p: REMARKS
This Amendment is responsive to the Office Action dated September 20, 2023.
Applicant has amended claims 1, 18, 27, and 29, and canceled claim 12. Claims 1, 3-5, 7, 8, 10, 11, 13-18, 20, 21, 23, 24, and 26-32 are pending upon entry of this communication.
The Office Action rejected previously presented claims 1, 3-5, 7, 8, 10-18, 20, 21, 23, 24, and 26-32 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as follows:
" Claims 1, 3-5, 7, 8, 10-16, 18, 20, 21, 23, 24, and 26-32 were rejected as allegedly being
unpatentable over U.S. Publication No. 2005/0115561 Al by Stahmann et al.
(hereinafter, "Stahmann") in view of U.S. Publication No. 2010/0121399 Al by McCabe et al., (hereinafter, "McCabe"), further in view of U.S. Publication No. 2005/0148896 Al
by Siejko et al. (hereinafter, "Siejko"), and further in view of U.S. Publication No.
2011/0009760 Al by Zhang et al. (hereinafter, "Zhang"); and
" Claim 17 was rejected as allegedly being unpatentable over Stahmann in view of
McCabe, further in view of Zhang, further in view of Siejko, further in view of U.S.
Publication No. 2012/0283705 Al by Lee et al. (hereinafter, "Lee").

Applicant respectfully traverses the rejections to the extent the rejections may be considered applicable to the claims as amended. The applied references, alone or in any combination, fail to disclose or suggest the features defined by Applicant's claims, and there would have been no apparent reason that would have caused one of ordinary skill in the art to modify the applied references to arrive at the claimed features.
For example, the applied references fail to disclose or suggest a system comprising

"processing circuitry of at least one of [an] insertable cardiac monitor or [a] remote computing device, the processing circuitry configured to: periodically determine a respective value for each of a plurality of physiological parameters based on one or more of the heart sounds or the ECG, wherein at least a first physiological parameter of the plurality of physiological parameters is determined based on the heart sounds and at least a second physiological parameter of the plurality of physiological parameters is determined based on the ECG, wherein the first physiological parameter comprises a frequency of occurrence of an S3 heart sound; ... and determine whether to present an indication of a heart failure event based on an analysis of the

trends of the periodically determined values of the physiological parameters, wherein to perform the analysis of the trends the processing circuitry is configured to: determine a first variation value of at least one physiological parameter of the plurality of physiological parameters for a first period and a second variation value of the at least one of the physiological parameter for a second period preceding the first period; and determine whether a comparison of the first variation value and the second variation value satisfies a criterion," as recited by amended independent claim 1, or the similar recitations of amended independent claims 18, 27, and 29.

In rejecting previously presented claim 12, which recited a different feature of "the processing circuitry is configured to determine whether a change of at least one of the physiological parameters in a period is significantly greater than a variation in the physiological parameter during prior periods," the Office Action cited FIGS. 62A-N, Table 2, and paragraphs [0109], [0221], [0288], and [0295] of Stahmann, and paragraph [0061] of Zhang. While some of the cited portions of Stahmann discuss heart rate variability, they do so on the context of disordered breathing, rather than a determination of whether to present an indication of a heart failure event. For example, paragraph [0295] of Stahmann states "sleep disordered breathing is also associated with a number of secondary or chronic responses, including, for example, chronic decrease in heart rate variability (HRV) .. .." Such a description suggests neither a determination of whether to present an indication of a heart failure event, nor processing circuitry configured to: "determine a first variation value of at least one physiological parameter of the plurality of physiological parameters for a first period and a second variation value of the at least one of the physiological parameter for a second period preceding the first period; and determine whether a comparison of the first variation value and the second variation value satisfies a criterion," as recited in amended claim 1.

Paragraph [0061] of Zhang, on the other hand, states "[d]etecting a deterioration of the patient's heart failure status may involve comparing the change in the collected physiologic data to a threshold comprising at least one of a predetermined change in the collected physiologic data, a predetermined rate of change in the collected physiologic data, and a predetermined variance in the collected physiologic data." However, generally comparing a change in data to a threshold is not the same as or even suggestive of processing circuitry configured to: "determine a first variation value of at least one physiological parameter of the plurality of physiological parameters for a first period and a second variation value of the at least one of the physiological

parameter for a second period preceding the first period; and determine whether a comparison of the first variation value and the second variation value satisfies a criterion," as recited in amended claim 1, or the similar recitations of the other independent claims.
For at least the reasons discussed above, independent claims 1, 18, 27, and 29, are
patentable over the applied references. The dependent claims incorporate the requirements of the respective independent claims.1 Accordingly, the dependent claims are likewise patentable.

For at least these reasons, the Office Action has failed to establish aprimafacie case for non-patentability of Applicant's claims 1, 3-5, 7, 8, 10, 11, 13-18, 20, 21, 23, 24, and 26-32 under 35 U.S.C. § 103. Applicant therefore respectfully requests reconsideration and withdrawal of this rejection.
CONCLUSION
All claims in this application are in condition for allowance. Applicant does not

acquiesce as to any assertion in the Office Action with respect to the cited art or to Applicant's claims. Applicant's silence with respect to any assertion in the Office Action should not be interpreted as Applicant's acquiescence thereto. Applicant reserves the right to comment further with respect to the applied references and any pending claim in a future Amendment, Response, or on appeal. Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration and prompt allowance of all pending claims.

Applicant does not concede that the subject matter encompassed by the claims prior to this Amendment is unpatentable over the art cited by the Office Action. While several distinctions have been noted over the art of record, Applicant notes that there may be several other limitations that are neither taught nor suggested by the art of record. Applicant expressly reserves all rights and arguments with respect to distinctions not explicitly noted herein. In addition, to the extent that amendments included herein constitute a narrowing of the claims, such narrowing of the claims should not be construed as an admission as to the merits of the prior rejections. Indeed, Applicant traverses the rejections and preserves all rights and arguments. To the extent that any particular statement or argument by the Office in the pending Office Action has not been explicitly addressed herein, the same should not be construed as an acquiescence or admission by the Applicant that such statements or arguments by the Office are accurate and proper.
